_about: Dean & Neligh (2023), experiment 1.2 (Changing Incentives), with 10 questions per treatment instead of 50. Treatment ids follow the paper's numbering of the decision problems (DPs 3-6). Payoffs are dollars: the paper's 5, 40, 70 and 95 probability points are $2, $16, $28 and $38 here ($40 x points / 100, the expected value with the paper's $40 prize), and the practice question's 10/0, 5/5 points are $4/$0, $2/$2, and only one student is paid: one student is drawn at random, then one of their main questions. Settings whose names start with an underscore, like this one, are notes and are ignored.
